name: Vibrant Purple
lede: Vibrant Purple is the modifier "vibrant" applied to [[purple]], recorded only in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey, with no earlier listing in our sources.

sections.title: An intensity modifier
sections.body:
The name combines the intensity modifier "vibrant" with the base color [[purple]]; our data has no record of it before the xkcd 2010 crowd survey [1]. No book or dictionary in our sources files it under an older name.

Its nearest look-alikes are [[dark-orchid]] (3.8 units, duller), [[purple-munsell]] (4.3, duller and darker) and [[dark-violet]] (4.9, darker); [[vivid-purple]] sits at the same distance as Dark Violet but reads more vivid rather than less [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed; a color this saturated is rare in aged, varnished paint [3]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 45, chroma 106 and hue 320 degrees, among the most saturated entries in our purple family [3].

origin.named_after: a modifier ("vibrant") on the base color purple

questions.q: Vibrant Purple's name combines which modifier with purple?
True or false: our archive has paintings where Vibrant Purple covers a meaningful share of the canvas.

openers: Vibrant Purple is too saturated to show up in any painting in our archive.
